chapter: Bennie Moten, Basie and the Reno
title: Fairyland Park and Moten's two pianos
summary: Back from Wichita, Moten played Fairyland Park, the best job in town at $57 a week, with two baby grands and Basie on payroll.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did Bill Saunders come back with him?
Bill Saunders wasn't with the band.
He wasn't with the band?
Not then.
Benny came back to Kansas City by himself?
No, he came back with the band.
With the band?

They finished the engagement in Wichita. They had commitments in Fairlawn Park in Kansas City, which was about the best job in town. This was about the best paying job or big paying. You played there nightly, seven nights a week. I think the salary for a sideman, and I worked there about three different times, I think the salary for a sideman was $57.00 per week, and this was the biggest money.
Yeah, that's where Andy Kirk got his start.
Well I don't know if Andy ever worked at Fairlawn Maryland.
Oh yes, yeah. Well, I'm pretty sure he did. Of course I shouldn't be able to tell you anything.
I don't know.
In all the biographies of him it says he was there.
He might have played there one summer but I remember --
Well anyway, the band, Benny Moten's band came back with Basie in tow, right?
With Basie. When they set up out at Fairlawn Park, Benny had two pianos, two baby grands on the stand. Basie played piano with the band.
That was Moten, he set Basie up with a piano?
He set Basie up and he had two pianos.
And put him on the payroll, full payroll?
Put him on the payroll.
That was the first thing with the Molton band, full payroll and a full member of the band?
Right.
